name: Dennis Sullivan's house, 134 DeKoven Street
research_note: DENNIS SULLIVAN'S HOUSE, built by T-3689 for the 1871 scene: the house across DeKoven Street from the O'Learys, at No. 134. Sullivan, sitting by the fence in front of it, was the first to see the fire in the barn across the street and ran to it (Andreas vol. 2, p. 708). The fire ran north and east and the houses on the south side of the street stood.

documented_range.note: Standing on the night of the fire (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 707-715); when it was built is not known, and the scene's phase begins in 1860.

position.symbolic_location: 134 DeKoven Street, south side, nearly opposite the O'Learys.
position.note: On the 1871 plan's south building line, its front to the street, nearly opposite the O'Leary lot (Andreas vol. 2, p. 708: 'nearly opposite the O'Leary place'). The footprint's origin is local E -310.45 N -1974.85.

derivation.reason: Laid out from Andreas's measured description of the lots against the 1871 plan's DeKoven Street; no traced frontage for the 1871 city is in data/traces/street_control.json to recompute it from.

blocks.name: Sullivan's house
blocks.note: Dennis Sullivan's house at No. 134, 'nearly opposite the O'Leary place' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 708); its size and finish are reconstructed.

fire.note: South of DeKoven Street, against the wind: the fire ran north and east from the barn (Andreas vol. 2, p. 708).
